PUBLIC BUSINESS FROM THE FLOOR - AGENDIZED ITEMS
Any person who would like to address the Legislative Bodies on any agendized item is requested to complete a speaker card for the City Clerk/Agency/Authority Secretary and identify the agenda item you would like to discuss.   Each person will be given an opportunity to address the Legislative Body at the time such item is discussed.  Speaker cards are available at the rear of the Council Chambers and your speaker card must be filled out prior to the agenda item being called. We respectfully request that you fill the cards out completely and print as clearly as possible. Following this procedure will allow for a smooth and timely process for the meeting and we appreciate your cooperation. Individual speakers are limited to three (3) minutes each.
Consent Calendar items under the Legislative Body may be acted upon with one motion, a second and the vote. If you desire to speak on an item or items on the Consent Calendar, you may fill out one speaker card for the Consent Calendar. You will be given three minutes to address your concerns before the Legislative Body takes action on the Consent Calendar.

SUCCESSOR AGENCY ACTIONS
CONSENT CALENDAR
SA CC 1. Approve the purchase and sale agreement with GAFY Investments for the sale of APN 3114-010-900.
GAFY Investments has made an offer for APN 3114-010-900, a 2.5-acre parcel located in the Fox Field Industrial Corridor. The parcel is landlocked and unimproved. The property is designated for liquidation under the approved Long-Range Property Management Plan (LRPMP). GAFY’s is the first and only offer received on the property to date. Sale of the parcel is consistent with the LRPMP previously approved by the Oversight Board and the State of California Department of Finance.
SA CC1
SA CC1 attachment
SA CC 2. Approve the purchase and sale agreement with Resolution Fund Management LLC for the sale of various irregular parcels located in the Fox Field Industrial Corridor.
The area in question represents a significant challenge in terms of site assembly, as the parcels are highly irregular; they were permitted to be heavily subdivided prior to the City of Lancaster’s incorporation; and the lots are unimproved. In order to create a viable site from the affected parcels, a number of adjacent parcels would first need to be acquired from various private parties. As such, interest in purchasing the parcels has been limited. Resolution Fund Management’s is the first and only offer received on the property to date. The parcels are designated for liquidation under the approved Long-Range Property Management Plan (LRPMP); thus, their sale is consistent with the LRPMP previously approved by the Oversight Board and the State of California Department of Finance
SA CC 2
SA CC 2 attachment
NEW BUSINESS
SA NB 1. Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the Period July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020
Recommendation:
Adopt Resolution No. SA 01-19, approving the Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the period July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020 and directing staff to bring before the County of Los Angeles Consolidated Oversight Board for approval.
Health & Safety Code Section 34177(o)(1) requires the Successor Agencies of the previous Redevelopment Agencies to prepare Recognized Obligation Payment Schedules (ROPS) that list obligations to be paid for the coming July 1 to June 30. These schedules are used by the County Auditor-Controller in determining the amount of property tax revenues to distribute to the Successor Agency.
SA NB 1
SA NB 1 attachment
SA NB 2. Successor Agency Administrative Budgets for the Periods July 1, 2019 to December 31, 2019 and January 1, 2020 to June 30, 2020
Recommendation:
Adopt Resolution No. SA 02-19, approving the Successor Agency Administrative Budgets for the periods of July 1, 2019 to December 31, 2019 and January 1, 2020 to June 30, 2020, as detailed in Attachments A & B.
Health and Safety Code Section 34177(j) requires Successor Agencies to adopt six month budgets. These budgets are developed from the enforceable obligations listed on the Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the period July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020.

JCC 1. Approve Loan Agreement between City of Lancaster and the California Choice Energy Authority
City Council Recommendation:
Approve Loan Agreement between the City of Lancaster and the California Choice Energy Authority and authorize the City Mayor, or designee, to execute all necessary documents.
California Choice Energy Authority Recommendation:
Approve Loan Agreement between the City of Lancaster and the California Choice Energy Authority and authorize the Board Chairman, or designee, to execute all necessary documents.
Approval of the loan agreement between the City of Lancaster and the CCEA will provide cash flow and operating reserve, while CCEA builds up its own reserve. CCEA will repay the principal and all accrued interest on any loaned funds as funds become available during the term of the agreement, but in no case later than 24 months from date of loan.
JCC 1

JCC 2. Assignment of Professional Service Agreements with Braun, Blaising, Smith & Wynn, PC from City of Lancaster to California Choice Energy Authority
City Council Recommendation:
Approve the assignment of professional services agreement with Braun, Blaising, Smith & Wynn, PC ("BBSW") to California Choice Energy Authority ("CCEA); and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute all necessary documents.
California Choice Energy Authority Recommendation:
Accept the assignment of professional services agreement with Braun, Blaising, Smith & Wynn, PC ("BBSW") from City of Lancaster; and authorize the Executive Director, or his designee, to execute all necessary documents.
On July 10, 2018, Council approved an agreement between BBSW and City of Lancaster for BBSW to provide regulatory legal services. These services include representing the City of Lancaster, Lancaster Choice Energy (LCE), and CCEA before the California Public Utilities Commission ("CPUC"). BBSW advises staff regarding pending and/or anticipated CPUC matters, rate cases, and rule changes that may affect LCE's and/or CCEA's interests. They also assist in the preparation and submission of required regulatory compliance filings at the CPUC and the California Energy Commission.

JCC 3. Amendment 3 to Administrative Services Agreement between City of Lancaster and California Choice Energy Authority
City Council Recommendation:
Approve Amendment 3 to Administrative Services Agreement with California Choice Energy Authority ("CCEA"); and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute all necessary documents.
California Choice Energy Authority Recommendation:
Approve Amendment 3 to Administrative Services Agreement with the City of Lancaster ("Lancaster"); and authorize the Executive Director, or his designee, to execute all necessary documents.
Under the terms of this Agreement, CCEA will provide operational support and work with various consultants in support of Lancaster's CCA operations.

JCC 4. Approve Security Agreement, Account Control Agreement, and Intercreditor and Collateral Agency Agreement with River City Bank
City Council Recommendation:
a. Approve Security Agreement between the City of Lancaster and River City Bank for the benefit of Power Purchase Providers, as Secured Creditors; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute all necessary documents.
b. Approve Account Control Agreement between the City of Lancaster and River City Bank for the benefit of Power Purchase Providers, as Secured Creditors; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute all necessary documents.
c. Approve Intercreditor and Collateral Agency Agreement between the City of Lancaster, and River City Bank; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute all necessary documents.
d. Ratify the termination of Security Agreement, Account Control, and Intercreditor and Collateral Agency Agreements between the City of Lancaster and Wilmington Trust, National Association effective February 28, 2019; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute all necessary documents.
California Choice Energy Authority Recommendation:
Approve Intercreditor and Collateral Agency Agreement between California Choice Energy Authority, on behalf of City of Lancaster, and River City Bank; and authorize the Executive Director, or his designee, to execute all necessary documents.
Through the Professional Services Agreements and Administrative Services Agreements, CCEA will facilitate the purchase and sale of electricity and other related services on behalf of member cities. The Professional Services Agreement between the City and CCEA will provide a means of utilizing City staff and regulatory services in support of the agreements. In order to be consistent with CCEA's member cities securities, staff requests that Council approve the transfer of the City of Lancaster's lockbox from Wilmington Trust National Association to River City Bank.
JCC 4
JCC 4 attachment
CCEA CC 1. Award contract to Bayshore Consulting Group, Inc. for management, operations, and administrative services for the California Choice Energy Authority; and authorize the Board Chairman, or his designee, to execute all necessary documents.
Due to staffing reductions and a desire to expand in the Southern California territory, the CCEA desires to contract with a firm(s) to manage and provide oversight of the functional areas of CCEA including finance, regulatory and legislative affairs, power procurement, contract administration, and overall operations. From October 9, 2018 to November 8, 2018, the CCEA solicited information and proposals from qualified firms (or combination of firms) for the professional services related to the management, administration, and operations of CCEA. On November 8, 2018, at 5:00 p.m., the City recorded one (1) sealed bid package received. Sealed bids were given to an evaluation committee for review to establish respondent not only met the minimum requirements, but also met specific criteria as stated in the proposal document. The Bayshore Consulting Group, Inc. received a satisfactory evaluation score and has been selected as the recommended consultant.
CCEA CC1
CCEA CC1 attachment
CC 1. Waive further reading of any proposed ordinances. (This permits reading the title only in lieu of reciting the entire text.)
CC 2. Approve the Check and Wire Registers for November 11, 2018 through December 8, 2018 in the amount of $10,432,275.13. Approve the Check Registers as presented.
At each regular City Council Meeting, the City Council is presented with check and ACH/wire registers listing the financial claims (invoices) against the City for purchase of materials, supplies, services, and capital projects issued the prior three to four weeks. This process provides the City Council the opportunity to review the expenditures of the City. Claims are paid via checks, Automated Clearing House (ACH) payments, or federal wires. The justifying backup information for each expenditure is available in the Finance Department.
CC 2
CC 2 attachment
CC 3. Accept and approve the November 2018, Monthly Report of Investments as submitted.
Each month, the Finance Department prepares a report listing the investments for all separate entities under the jurisdiction of the City as identified in the City’s Comprehensive Annual Financial Report.
CC 3
CC 3 attachment
CC 4. Adopt Resolution No. 19-01, directing and authorizing the street name change of Avenue N to R. Lee Ermey Avenue / Avenue N, from Sierra Highway to Agena Road.
As an area-wide tribute, the County of Los Angeles, and the City of Palmdale have approved the name change of Avenue N to R. Lee Ermey Avenue I Avenue N to recognize this local hero. In order to maintain consistency, staff is recommending co-naming Avenue N with the County of Los Angeles and the City of Palmdale. There are approximately 32 vacant lots along Avenue N with only 9 addresses assigned. These 9 addresses will not be affected during this processes as co-naming Avenue N allows residents continued use of their current addresses. Caltrans signs along the freeway will be modified at a later time.
CC 4
CC 4 attachment
PUBLIC HEARING
PH 1. Economic Development Agreement with Golden State Procurement Company, Inc.
Recommendation:
Adopt Resolution No. 19-02, approving an Economic Development Agreement with Golden State Procurement Company, Inc.; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute all related documents.
The City of Lancaster has a long-standing agreement with Cardlock Fuels, the most recent of which is an Amended and Restated Sublease dated November 2010. Cardlock recently assigned its rights under the existing agreement to Golden State Procurement Company, Inc. The proposed Economic Development Agreement would provide for a sales tax rebate of up to 15% from the City of Lancaster for any new sales tax revenue generated under the agreement. This rebate aims to attract increased sales tax revenue to the City of Lancaster.
